findings.category: Task ordering and live-resource gate inconsistency
findings.location: plan.md lines 638-645, 768-775, 931-940; research.md lines 476-489; quickstart.md lines 3-27; contracts/release-verification-contract.md lines 3-8 and 317-327; tasks.md lines 174-194
findings.affected_requirement: Full Story Flow analyze-before-implement ordering, T064-T071 transient RED/GREEN boundary, T072 sole live release run, and T073 cleanup/final verification
findings.evidence: The regenerated tasks authority makes T064-T071 non-live Option A RED/GREEN and verification work, explicitly forbids live Docker/PostgreSQL/provider/Repository/Playwright acquisition through T071, assigns the sole live Windows Docker Desktop/PostgreSQL run to T072 only after fresh Full analysis, separate accepted reviews, and clean-candidate pinning, and assigns independent cleanup/final verification to T073. The accepted plan set still directs completion of T064/T065 as the remaining work, calls T064 the Windows Docker Desktop host and the only lane allowed to execute the live lifecycle, labels the release contract a T064 contract, and says regenerated work proceeds through remaining T064/T065 evidence. These raw authorities therefore identify different task IDs and prerequisites for live external-resource acquisition. Following the plan or quickstart literally can bypass the T064-T071 non-live RED/GREEN sequence and T072 review/candidate gates; following tasks makes the plan-set task references false.
findings.correction_outcome: After explicit user approval, align only the complete accepted plan set's current task references and execution directions with regenerated tasks.md: T064-T071 are the non-live Option A RED/GREEN and verification boundary, T072 is the sole live Windows Docker Desktop/PostgreSQL/Playwright run after its stated fresh gates and clean-candidate pin, and T073 owns independent cleanup/final verification. Preserve historical references to the prior failed live T064 only when clearly labeled historical, preserve the accepted Option A topology and all hashes/authorization history, regenerate any dependent task artifact if its authority changes, and rerun fresh read-only analysis before implementation.
